items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: As a matter of fact I was a nobody on the band compared to Randy Brecker and Faddis and those people.

ctx.x: He always started out, like we had this party in Tokyo when we first got there and Woody Herman was there with Flip Phillips and Al Cohn and I don’t know if Zoot was there. All-star Woody Herman band or some pick-up band. And Kai Winding was there with J.J. Johnson. It was a big thing in Japan where we all came together at the end in Yokohama and put on this huge concert. But after this feast, it was a feast, we all went our separate ways on the road so to speak in Japan, and then we all met at the end of about a…

know what I mean? And the last thing I want to say about Jaco, because I thought the world of him musically and I thought the world of him personally too, deep down he was a really nice, generous, giving person. As a matter of fact I was a nobody on the band compared to Randy Brecker and Faddis and those people. And one night just he and I hung out together. He wasn’t into this — he was like — he wasn’t into this thing of just hanging out with his star soloists, you know like Mintzer and Randy Brecker and Faddis,…
I have not read it yet.

items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: on “Born to Run” the Bruce Springsteen record. It was me, Mike and Sanborn and a great trombone player, Wayne Andre.

ctx.x: And if it was not professionally done then you had to do some scrambling?

Well yeah, we had to do some writing sometimes, and on some very good records. This one always comes to mind, on “Born to Run” the Bruce Springsteen record. It was me, Mike and Sanborn and a great trombone player, Wayne Andre. We showed up at the session and there was music paper on our stands but they were blank. And I think they might have had some bar lines but sometimes they didn’t even have bar lines. So it became our job to write a chart. And this was a little out of our — I’ll never forget it — “Tenth…
This is very interesting for me because I’ve played that song with different bands so to hear that thing and remember that I’ve played [scats]. That’s great.
